sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Every town or city has its own regional celebrity who everyone recognizes.
sentences.zh: 每个城镇或城市都有自己家喻户晓的地区名人。

sentences.en: Maybe that person is a high school athlete who made it to the major leagues.
sentences.zh: 也许那个人是打进职业大联盟的高中运动员。

sentences.en: Maybe they're a titan of industry.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是工业巨头。

sentences.en: Maybe they're a flamboyant attorney with an excessive amount of billboard ads.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是一位广告牌多得离谱的浮夸律师。

sentences.en: Something wrong?
sentences.zh: 有什么不对吗？

sentences.en: Call Ann Fong.
sentences.zh: 给安·方打电话。

sentences.en: Some of them become so successful that their acclaim spreads around the world.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人非常成功，以至于他们的名声传遍了世界。

sentences.en: And sometimes not.
sentences.zh: 但有时却并非如此。

sentences.en: Here to tell us about one of her own favorite local celebrities is actress, reporter, and friend of the show, Gillian Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 今天来为我们介绍她最喜欢的当地名人之一的是演员、记者，也是本节目的朋友，吉莉安·雅各布斯。

sentences.en: Hey, Gillian.
sentences.zh: 嘿，吉莉安。

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗨，罗曼。

sentences.en: It's so delightful to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: I'm delighted as well.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴。

sentences.en: It's my favorite place to be.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢待的地方。

sentences.en: So, Gillian, you reached out to us because you wanted to talk about a very specific, famous face that you saw all over your hometown.
sentences.zh: 那么，吉莉安，你联系我们是因为你想聊聊你在家乡随处可见的一张非常特别的著名面孔。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I come from the great city of Pittsburgh, also known as Pittsburgh to locals.
sentences.zh: 我来自伟大的匹兹堡市，当地人也称之为“匹兹堡”。

sentences.en: And there was a guy who was so famous there that I thought everyone knew his name.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个人非常出名，我以为每个人都知道他的名字。

sentences.en: And it turns out that's not quite the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So who is this mysterious local celebrity?
sentences.zh: 那么这位神秘的当地名人是谁呢？

sentences.en: I'm going to leave you in suspense for a little bit longer.
sentences.zh: 我要让你再悬念一会儿。

sentences.en: So just to back up and explain, this guy recently popped into my head because a few months ago I was at home watching a football game, which is not common practice for me,
sentences.zh: 回过头来解释一下，这个人最近突然出现在我的脑海里，因为几个月前我在家看一场橄榄球比赛，这对我来说并不常见，

sentences.en: read Taylor Swift.
sentences.zh: 读作泰勒·斯威夫特。

sentences.en: But as I was watching the game, I noticed that one of the players had something on his helmet.
sentences.zh: 但当我在看比赛时，我注意到其中一名球员的头盔上有些东西。

sentences.en: It was this little round green sticker.
sentences.zh: 那是一个圆形的小绿贴纸。

sentences.en: And I was thinking, why am I drawn to this little green circular sticker on the back of his head?
sentences.zh: 我在想，为什么我会被他脑后这个绿色的小圆贴纸吸引呢？

sentences.en: And staring at it unleashed this voice in my head.
sentences.zh: 盯着它看，我脑海里冒出了一个声音。

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck is me.
sentences.zh: “厌恶先生”就是我。

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck is green.
sentences.zh: “厌恶先生”是绿色的。

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck.
sentences.zh: “厌恶先生”。

sentences.en: I thought that the football player was wearing a Mr. Yuck sticker.
sentences.zh: 我以为那个橄榄球运动员贴的是“厌恶先生”的贴纸。

sentences.en: And it turns out I was not even close.
sentences.zh: 结果我完全猜错了。

sentences.en: That sticker means that a player is allowed to communicate with the sidelines via a radio in his helmet.
sentences.zh: 那个贴纸的意思是球员可以通过头盔里的无线电与场边进行沟通。

sentences.en: But it still sent me down this deep rabbit hole of why Mr. Yuck was so deeply embedded into my psyche that I was seeing him on the back of a football player's head.
sentences.zh: 但这还是让我陷入了深思：为什么“厌恶先生”如此深刻地植入我的潜意识，以至于我在橄榄球运动员的后脑勺上都能看到他？

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck, why indeed, why indeed?
sentences.zh: “厌恶先生”，为什么呢，到底为什么？

sentences.en: Have you ever heard of Mr. Yuck?
sentences.zh: 你听说过“厌恶先生”吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 听说过。

sentences.en: I am familiar with Mr. Yuck because he showed up briefly on this episode that we did years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 我很熟悉“厌恶先生”，因为他曾短暂出现在我们多年前做过的一期节目中。

sentences.en: But I also recognize him because I was a kid alive in the Midwest in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 但我认识他也是因为我是在20世纪80年代中西部长大的孩子。

sentences.en: Central Ohio for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说是俄亥俄州中部。

sentences.en: But for people who are not Midwestern Gen Xers, who is Mr. Yuck?
sentences.zh: 但对于那些不是中西部X世代的人来说，“厌恶先生”是谁？

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck is a neon green circular sticker with a cartoon face on it.
sentences.zh: “厌恶先生”是一个带有卡通脸的荧光绿色圆形贴纸。

sentences.en: His face is scrunched up with his eyes squeezed tight and his tongue is sticking out of its mouth.
sentences.zh: 他的脸皱在一起，眼睛紧闭，舌头从嘴里伸出来。

sentences.en: It's the face you make when you taste something disgusting.
sentences.zh: 这就是你尝到恶心东西时做的表情。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's the pictorial embodiment of the sentiment of yuck.
sentences.zh: 没错，他是“厌恶”这种情绪的具象化体现。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's a symbol for hazardous substances aimed at deterring children from ingesting them.
sentences.zh: 他是一个危险物质的标志，旨在阻止儿童误食。

sentences.en: He was basically created to indicate that if you saw a Mr. Yuck sticker on something, it meant that that something was poison.
sentences.zh: 他基本上就是为了提醒你，如果你在某样东西上看到“厌恶先生”的贴纸，就意味着那东西有毒。

sentences.en: Do not ingeSt.
sentences.zh: 禁止食用。

sentences.en: And I grew up thinking he was as famous as Smokey Bear.
sentences.zh: 我从小就以为他像斯莫基熊一样出名。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if I remember correctly,
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，

sentences.en: parents would get these sheets of the Mr. Yuck stickers and stick them on dangerous stuff like drain cleaner or whatever a kid could get his hands on underneath the sink.
sentences.zh: 父母会拿到这些“厌恶先生”的贴纸，把它们贴在排水管清洁剂之类的危险物品上，或者任何孩子在水槽下能拿到的东西上。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So Mr. Yuck was created in 1971 by a physician named Dr. Richard Moriarty, who was a pediatrician and the founder of the Pittsburgh Poison Center.
sentences.zh: “厌恶先生”是由一位名叫理查德·莫里亚蒂的医生在1971年创造的，他是一位儿科医生，也是匹兹堡毒物中心的创始人。

sentences.en: And as the head of the Pittsburgh Poison Center, he wanted to accomplish two different things.
sentences.zh: 作为匹兹堡毒物中心的负责人，他想实现两个不同的目标。

sentences.en: One, he wanted to prevent kids from ingesting potentially dangerous substances.
sentences.zh: 第一，他想防止儿童误食潜在的危险物质。

sentences.en: And two, he wanted to teach parents that when their kids did ingest a potentially dangerous substance, to call a poison control center before rushing them to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 第二，他想教导父母，当孩子误食了潜在危险物质时，在送往医院之前先打电话给毒物控制中心。

sentences.en: Because there was a good chance that the kid would be just fine.
sentences.zh: 因为孩子很有可能并无大碍。

sentences.en: And calling poison control could save you a lot of time and money.
sentences.zh: 而拨打毒物控制中心电话可以为你节省大量的时间和金钱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just generally save taxpayer money, too.
sentences.zh: 而且通常也能节省纳税人的钱。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Roman, in your tenure as a parent, have you ever had to call poison control?
sentences.zh: 那么，罗曼，在你为人父母的这段时间里，你有没有打过毒物控制中心的电话？

sentences.en: No, thankfully, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，谢天谢地，没有。

sentences.en: No, not with any of my children.
sentences.zh: 没有，我的孩子们都没有过。

sentences.en: But I have always been fascinated by the poison control hotline because basically it's this type of very low ambition free health care service that you can call anytime for a very specific kind of medical advice.
sentences.zh: 但我一直对毒物控制热线很着迷，因为它基本上是一种非常低门槛的免费医疗服务，你可以随时拨打它来获取非常具体的医疗建议。

sentences.en: So I've always wondered how that came to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直很好奇它是怎么来的。

sentences.en: Well, Roman, you are a very lucky man because I'm here to tell you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，罗曼，你是个非常幸运的人，因为我来告诉你。

sentences.en: So poison centers are actually a pretty recent phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 毒物中心其实是一个相当近期的现象。

sentences.en: Until the 19th century, we mostly had to rely on conspicuous packaging and poison labels for poison prevention.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪，我们主要还是依靠显眼的包装和毒物标签来进行防毒。

sentences.en: Apothecaries were required to store hazardous substances in irregularly shaped bottles so they wouldn't be mixed up with the other products.
sentences.zh: 药剂师被要求将危险物质储存在形状不规则的瓶子里，以免与其他产品混淆。

sentences.en: And also in the mid-1800s,
sentences.zh: 而且在19世纪中期，

sentences.en: it became mandated by the American Pharmaceutical Association to clearly label a bottle with the word poison or with the medically accepted poison symbol at the time.
sentences.zh: 美国药学协会强制要求在瓶子上清楚地标明“毒药”字样，或使用当时医学界公认的毒药符号。

sentences.en: And that poison symbol being the skull and crossbones.
sentences.zh: 那个毒药符号就是骷髅和交叉骨。

sentences.en: You got it.
sentences.zh: 你说对了。

sentences.en: But by the time we rolled around to the end of the 19th and early 20th century, there actually still wasn't a ton else being done in terms of preventative poison control,
sentences.zh: 但到了19世纪末和20世纪初，在预防性毒物控制方面其实并没有做太多工作，

sentences.en: which was a huge problem because around then, a brand new danger was entering American homes.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的问题，因为那时一种全新的危险正在进入美国家庭。

sentences.en: Mr. Clean gets rid of dirt and grime and grease in just a minute.
sentences.zh: “清洁先生”一分钟内就能清除污垢、油垢和油脂。

sentences.en: Mr. Clean will clean your...
sentences.zh: “清洁先生”将清洁你的……

sentences.en: Ah, yes, the dastardly Mr. Clean, the worst of all.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的，卑鄙的“清洁先生”，最糟糕的一个。

sentences.en: Now, I don't want to blame everything on Mr. Clean, especially because he actually wasn't invented at this time.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不想把一切都归咎于“清洁先生”，尤其是因为他当时还没被发明出来。

sentences.en: But he and other package cleaners represented this huge cultural shift taking place in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 但他和其他包装清洁剂代表了20世纪初发生的巨大文化转变。

sentences.en: There was really an explosion of consumer product marketing and production.
sentences.zh: 消费品营销和生产确实出现了爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: And there were all sorts of products that were coming on the market, like vacuum cleaners, but also household cleaners that were pre-prepared and packaged.
sentences.zh: 市场上出现了各种各样的产品，比如吸尘器，还有预先准备好并包装好的家用清洁剂。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Marion Moser-Jones.
sentences.zh: 这位是玛丽恩·莫泽-琼斯博士。

sentences.en: She's an associate professor and historian of public health at Ohio State University.
sentences.zh: 她是俄亥俄州立大学的副教授和公共卫生历史学家。

sentences.en: She says that at the turn of the 20th century, there was this whole chemical revolution taking place in the United States.
sentences.zh: 她说，在20世纪之交，美国发生了一场全面的化学革命。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, Americans developed a kind of obsession with cleanliness and hygiene.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，美国人对清洁和卫生产生了一种痴迷。

sentences.en: There was also a huge rise in mass production and advertising, which meant more of these pre-packaged cleaners ended up in homes around the U.S.
sentences.zh: 大规模生产和广告也出现了巨大的增长，这意味着更多的预包装清洁剂进入了美国家庭。

sentences.en: So suddenly, whereas before it might have been that in an average household, there might have been some lye soap or a couple of potential poisonous substances.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，虽然以前普通家庭里可能只有一些碱性肥皂或几种潜在的毒性物质，

sentences.en: Now, there were all of these packaged cleaners.
sentences.zh: 现在却有了所有这些包装好的清洁剂。

sentences.en: You had a floor cleaner or floor polish.
sentences.zh: 你有地板清洁剂或地板抛光剂。

sentences.en: But most of these products being marketed were not being labeled correctly.
sentences.zh: 但大多数被推销的产品都没有被正确标记。

sentences.en: So this was very prevalent in turn of the 20th century U.S.

sentences.en: society.
sentences.zh: 这些物质，这些被错误标记的产品，而且并没有真正的要求去标记它们。

sentences.en: These substances, these products that were mislabeled, and there wasn't really a requirement to label them.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你在制造某种产品，我的意思是，如果你的所有竞争对手都没有这样做，你为什么要给它贴上巨大的警告标志呢？

sentences.en: And certainly, if you were manufacturing some kind of product, I mean, why would you put a giant warning sign on it if all of your competitors are not?
sentences.zh: 我记得，我经历过一个美好的口号叫“通过化学实现更好的生活”，消费者要求家庭便利。

sentences.en: I can remember, and I lived through a time when there was a wonderful slogan called Better Living Through Chemistry, and consumers demanded household conveniences.
sentences.zh: 至少其中一些化学品和产品是有毒的。

sentences.en: And at least some of these chemicals and some of these products were toxic.
sentences.zh: 那么这是谁呢？

sentences.en: And so who is this?
sentences.zh: 这是艾伦·沃尔夫博士，他身兼数职，令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Alan Wolfe, and he wears many, many impressive hats.
sentences.zh: 其中两个身份是儿科医生和波士顿儿童医院儿科环境健康中心的联合主任。

sentences.en: And two of them are pediatrician and the co-director of the Pediatric Environmental Health Center at Boston Children's Hospital.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些新的清洁产品是由极其危险和有毒的化学物质组成的。

sentences.en: He says that these new cleaning products were made up of incredibly dangerous and toxic chemicals.
sentences.zh: 而且由于化工企业极力抵制适当的警告标签法规，

sentences.en: And because chemical companies really resisted proper warning label regulation,
sentences.zh: 儿童尤其成为了这一时期意外中毒的主要受害者。

sentences.en: it was children in particular who were the big victims of accidental poisonings during this time.
sentences.zh: 二战后和婴儿潮一代，许多婴儿和幼儿在20世纪40年代末和50年代初长大。

sentences.en: Kind of post-World War II and the baby boomer generation, a lot of infants and then toddlers came of age in the late 1940s and early 1950s.
sentences.zh: 中毒的高峰年龄在1岁到3岁之间。

sentences.en: And the peak age of poisoning is somewhere between one and three years of age.
sentences.zh: 而且危险家用物质的增加也不仅仅局限于清洁产品。

sentences.en: And that rise of dangerous household substances wasn't limited to cleaning products either.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代左右，制药行业推出了一种营销方案，当时听起来可能是一个好主意，

sentences.en: Around the 1940s, the pharmaceutical industry came out with a marketing scheme that probably at the time sounded like a great idea,

sentences.en: but was actually terrible in execution.

sentences.en: I'm old enough, Gillian, to remember taking candy aspirin.
sentences.zh: 它就是那样。

sentences.en: And it was just that.
sentences.zh: 它是橙子味的药片，对孩子非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: It was little.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的。

sentences.en: It was orange-flavored tablets and very attractive to children.
sentences.zh: 让我们把潜在的危险药物和糖果画上等号吧。

sentences.en: Ah, yes.
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能不出问题呢？

sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: What could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 呃，一个不太有趣的事实。

sentences.zh: 在糖果阿司匹林问世后的三年内，学龄前儿童占了阿司匹林死亡人数的80%。

sentences.en: Uh, not-so-fun fact.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.zh: 所以，家庭中涌入了大量危险产品，其中大多数没有被正确标记。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，如果孩子接触到了其中一种毒素，

sentences.en: So, there's this influx of dangerous products in homes, most of which are not labeled correctly.
sentences.zh: 许多医生甚至不知道如果儿童误食这些产品，什么剂量是致命的。

sentences.en: And on top of that, if a child got into one of those toxins,
sentences.zh: 没有人能把所有这些都记在脑子里。

sentences.en: many doctors didn't even know what or how much of those products would be lethal if ingested by children.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在新鞋盒里发现的那些用来保持鞋子干燥的小东西，毒性有多大，

sentences.en: No one could keep all this in their head.
sentences.zh: 那些小硅胶包？

sentences.zh: 那位刘易斯就是刘易斯·戈达尔曼，开发了第一个毒物控制中心的人。

sentences.zh: 他看到了中毒信息匮乏的问题，并决定为此做点什么。

sentences.zh: 他开始收集有关有毒物质的信息，并将其填写在这些小索引卡上。

sentences.en: And he saw this issue of a lack of information on poisonings and decided to do something about it.

sentences.en: And he sort of organized an informal referral service that people recognized him as an expert who was interested
sentences.zh: 以及应该如何处理。

sentences.en: and could talk to these families and talk to health care providers about what the poisonings were
sentences.zh: 他工作的圣卢克医院的医生开始咨询戈达尔曼，

sentences.en: and how they should be managed.
sentences.zh: 然后消息传到了芝加哥的其他医院，最终传到了其他城市。

sentences.en: Physicians at St. Luke's Hospital, where he worked, started consulting with Godalman
sentences.zh: 戈达尔曼会亲自在家中随时接听电话，无论白天还是黑夜。

sentences.en: and then word spread to other hospitals in Chicago and eventually to other cities.
sentences.zh: 但要成为一个单人乐队兼毒物百科全书真的很难。

sentences.en: Godalman would personally answer calls at any time, day or night, from his home.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终，戈达尔曼与爱德华·普雷斯博士一起，

sentences.en: But it's really hard to be a one-man band slash encyclopedia brown of poisons.
sentences.zh: 但要同时当一个单打独斗的乐队和毒物领域的“百科全书布朗”，真的很难。

sentences.en: So, eventually, Godalman, along with Dr. Edward Press,
sentences.zh: 所以最终，戈达尔曼与爱德华·普雷斯博士一起，

sentences.en: founded the first Poison Control Center in the United States in 1953.
sentences.zh: 于1953年在美国建立了第一个毒物控制中心。

sentences.en: So, that was the background for the start of the poison control movement in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是美国毒物控制运动起步的背景。

sentences.en: After that, Poison Control Centers started taking off like gangbusters.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，毒物控制中心开始如雨后春笋般迅速发展。

sentences.en: There was a huge number of centers opening up across the country throughout the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪60年代，全国各地涌现出大量的中心。

sentences.en: It kind of became a marketing technique for your local hospital.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上成了当地医院的一种营销手段。

sentences.en: Like, we have such high standards at our hospital.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们医院的标准非常高。

sentences.en: We have a Poison Control Center.
sentences.zh: 我们设有毒物控制中心。

sentences.en: So, in the 1960s, that really took hold so that by the mid-60s to late-60s,
sentences.zh: 所以，在20世纪60年代，这种做法真正流行起来，以至于到了60年代中后期，

sentences.en: there were over 600 poison centers in the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国已经有超过600个毒物中心了。

sentences.en: But, see, the problem with this influx of poison control centers
sentences.zh: 但是，你看，毒物控制中心激增带来的问题是，

sentences.en: was that the quality of care between the poison centers really could be inconsistent.
sentences.zh: 各毒物中心之间的护理质量确实参差不齐。

sentences.en: Some of them covered a neighborhood, a few thousand people.
sentences.zh: 有些中心只覆盖一个社区，服务几千人。

sentences.en: Others covered millions of people.
sentences.zh: 而另一些则覆盖数百万人。

sentences.en: Some of them were staffed by secretaries or pediatric and family practice,
sentences.zh: 有些中心由秘书、儿科医生、家庭医生、

sentences.en: health care providers, or trainees, whoever.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健提供者或实习生等人员配备，什么人都有。

sentences.en: So, there was a lot of variability, and there were complaints.
sentences.zh: 所以，差异性很大，也出现了不少投诉。

sentences.en: These were hard to reach.
sentences.zh: 这些中心很难联系上。

sentences.en: They weren't adequately staffed.
sentences.zh: 人员配备不足。

sentences.en: They weren't adequately publicized.
sentences.zh: 宣传也不到位。

sentences.en: And the information they gave was variable.
sentences.zh: 而且它们提供的信息也各不相同。

sentences.en: And this disjointed approach to poison centers was a really dangerous problem.
sentences.zh: 这种对毒物中心各自为政的处理方式是一个非常危险的问题。

sentences.en: Dr. Wolf actually worked as a poison center operator,
sentences.zh: 沃尔夫医生实际上曾担任过毒物中心接线员，

sentences.en: and he says that it's a really high-stress environment.
sentences.zh: 他说那是一个压力极大的环境。

sentences.en: When I was in the poison control center and talking to a parent,
sentences.zh: 当我在毒物控制中心与家长通话时，

sentences.en: and they were saying, my child just swallowed floor wax.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我的孩子刚吞下了地板蜡。

sentences.en: And so, you had to, you know, I had to juggle the microfiche reader
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须，你知道，我得一边操作缩微胶片阅读器，

sentences.en: and put in what the floor wax contained.
sentences.zh: 一边输入地板蜡的成分。

sentences.en: And then when you found out the detergents, you had to flip that out
sentences.zh: 当你查到洗涤剂成分后，你得把那张胶片取出来，

sentences.en: and flip in the other kind of management microfiche reader.
sentences.zh: 再换上另一种处理方法的缩微胶片。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the parent is holding online.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，家长还在电话那头等着。

sentences.en: He told me one story that really illustrated how important it was to have reliable care at these centers.
sentences.zh: 他给我讲了一个故事，真正说明了在这些中心提供可靠护理的重要性。

sentences.en: I remember a call I got at 7 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次早上7点接到一个电话，

sentences.en: one morning of two workers in Massachusetts
sentences.zh: 那天早上，马萨诸塞州有两名工人

sentences.en: who were found down at change of shift.
sentences.zh: 在换班时被发现倒在地上。

sentences.en: So these two men had been working in a chemical plant and were found unconscious.
sentences.zh: 这两名男子在化工厂工作，被发现时已经失去知觉。

sentences.en: Their job was to stir this sludge that was actually toxic discharge,
sentences.zh: 他们的工作是搅拌那些实际上是有毒废料的污泥，

sentences.en: and they weren't wearing protective gear.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有穿戴防护装备。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, this particular sludge contained a substance called propionitrile,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这种特殊的污泥含有一种叫丙腈的物质，

sentences.en: which when you inhale it, it's turned into cyanide.
sentences.zh: 吸入后会转化为氰化物。

sentences.en: So they were both suffering from cyanide poisoning.
sentences.zh: 所以他们两人都患上了氰化物中毒。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I know, it's horrific.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: But luckily in this case, Dr. Wolf, who is a trained specialist, was there to answer the call.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，在这种情况下，受过专业训练的沃尔夫医生正好接听了电话。

sentences.en: We recommended giving the cyanide antidote kit very quickly, and they were saved.
sentences.zh: 我们建议迅速使用氰化物解毒剂盒，他们因此获救了。

sentences.en: So in a situation like that, you really need someone who's highly trained to answer your call,
sentences.zh: 所以在那种情况下，你确实需要一个训练有素的人来接听你的电话，

sentences.en: which at the time, I mean, is kind of a roll of the dice
sentences.zh: 而在当时，这简直就像是在掷骰子，

sentences.en: because there are 600 different call centers with varying degrees of reliability.
sentences.zh: 因为有600个不同的呼叫中心，可靠程度各不相同。

sentences.en: Yes, and this was one of the big problems that Dr. Richard Moriarty, the father of Mr. Yuck, wanted to solve in 1971.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是“讨厌先生”（Mr. Yuck）之父理查德·莫里亚蒂医生在1971年想要解决的重大问题之一。

sentences.en: He wanted to find a way to make sure parents had the information of a trusted poison control center
sentences.zh: 他想找到一种方法，确保家长在孩子误食危险品时，

sentences.en: if their child ingested anything dangerous.
sentences.zh: 能获得值得信赖的毒物控制中心的信息。

sentences.en: Dr. Moriarty actually passed away in 2023, but this is a clip from an interview he did a few years before he died.
sentences.zh: 莫里亚蒂医生于2023年去世，但这片段摘自他去世前几年接受的一次采访。

sentences.en: We needed to get out the word that there was a for-real poison center for real people that were there 24 hours a day,
sentences.zh: 我们需要传达这样一个信息：有一个真正的毒物中心，为真正的人服务，全天24小时，

sentences.en: seven days a week, and they sort of knew what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 每周七天都在线，而且他们确实知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And if you had a problem, give us a buzz.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到问题，就给我们打个电话。

sentences.en: So we had to get our phone number out to the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须把我们的电话号码传遍世界。

sentences.en: On top of the lack of knowledge around reliable poison centers like the one he was running,
sentences.zh: 除了缺乏关于像他经营的那种可靠毒物中心的知识外，

sentences.en: Dr. Moriarty realized that there was a very unique problem that impacted the children of Pittsburgh specifically.
sentences.zh: 莫里亚蒂医生还意识到，有一个非常独特的问题影响着匹兹堡的孩子们。

sentences.en: Oh, what is that?
sentences.zh: 哦，那是什么？

sentences.en: So as you remember, the medically accepted warning symbol for poison since the 1800s was the skull and crossbones, right?
sentences.zh: 正如你所记得的，自19世纪以来，医学界公认的毒物警告标志是骷髅头和交叉骨，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, in Pittsburgh, that symbol carries a different connotation for kids.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在匹兹堡，这个标志对孩子们来说有不同的含义。

sentences.en: The traditional warning symbol was the skull and crossbones,
sentences.zh: 传统的警告标志是骷髅头和交叉骨，

sentences.en: which just happened to be part of the logo for the Pittsburgh Pirates and still is.
sentences.zh: 而这恰好是匹兹堡海盗队标志的一部分，现在依然如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, that doesn't make a whole heck of a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，这实在说不通。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's so true.
sentences.zh: 太对了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, we love our sports in Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在匹兹堡热爱体育运动。

sentences.en: You know, so the Pittsburgh Pirates, this is huge for us.
sentences.zh: 所以，匹兹堡海盗队，这对我们来说意义重大。

sentences.en: And there's a perhaps apocryphal story that the children of Pittsburgh would see a skull and crossbones image
sentences.zh: 有一个未经证实的说法是，匹兹堡的孩子们看到骷髅头和交叉骨的图像时，

sentences.en: and rather than think dangerous, poisonous, I must stay away,
sentences.zh: 他们不会想到危险、有毒、我必须远离，

sentences.en: they would think, oh, my beloved baseball team, you know,
sentences.zh: 而是会想，哦，我心爱的棒球队，你知道，

sentences.en: maybe this bottle of Windex is a Pittsburgh Pirates beverage.
sentences.zh: 也许这瓶玻璃清洁剂是匹兹堡海盗队的饮料。

sentences.en: So Dr. Moriarty had the idea to create a brand new symbol that would both spread awareness of the Pittsburgh Poison Center
sentences.zh: 所以莫里亚蒂医生想到了一个主意，创造一个全新的标志，既能提高匹兹堡毒物中心的知名度，

sentences.en: and was original and free from any other associations, one that would only and strictly mean do not eat.
sentences.zh: 又是原创的，没有任何其他联想，一个只代表“禁止食用”的标志。

sentences.en: He wanted something akin to Smokey Bear or McGrath the Crime Dog, anthropomorphized PSA.
sentences.zh: 他想要类似“斯莫基熊”或“犯罪克星麦格拉”那样拟人化的公益广告形象。

sentences.en: And Dr. Moriarty believed that for this symbol to be effective with children,
sentences.zh: 莫里亚蒂医生认为，要让这个标志对孩子们有效，

sentences.en: they needed to engage with them in the design process.
sentences.zh: 就必须让他们参与到设计过程中来。

sentences.en: And so he worked with a PR firm to pull together a focus group of kids.
sentences.zh: 于是他与一家公关公司合作，召集了一个儿童焦点小组。

sentences.en: And we started off basically with sort of preschool age kids and said to them,
sentences.zh: 我们基本上是从学龄前儿童开始，问他们：

sentences.en: if you got into a poison, what would happen to you?
sentences.zh: 如果你误食了毒药，你会怎么样？

sentences.en: And the recurring answers were, you die, you get sick, your mother would yell at you.
sentences.zh: 得到的重复回答是：你会死，你会生病，你妈妈会冲你大喊大叫。

sentences.en: OK, and we got those all pretty good things.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们得到了这些非常好的答案。

sentences.en: Accurate things.
sentences.zh: 准确的答案。

sentences.en: Good answers.
sentences.zh: 很好的回答。

sentences.en: So Moriarty worked with a guy named Dick Garber of the PR firm Vic Maitland and Associates,
sentences.zh: 所以莫里亚蒂与公关公司Vic Maitland and Associates的迪克·加伯合作，

sentences.en: and they interviewed children five and under and used their answers to come up with the design of the face and the color of the sticker.
sentences.zh: 他们采访了5岁及以下的孩子，并利用他们的回答设计出了表情和贴纸的颜色。

sentences.en: And this is the Mr. Yucksicker that you thought erroneously was on the back of a football player's helmet.
sentences.zh: 这就是你误以为印在橄榄球运动员头盔背后的“讨厌先生”贴纸。

sentences.en: The sort of the squinty face, the tongue, and it's like this bright fluorescent green.
sentences.zh: 那种斜视的表情，舌头，还有这种明亮的荧光绿。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the thought process behind the color was, which color will children like the least?
sentences.zh: 所以关于颜色的思考过程是：孩子们最不喜欢什么颜色？

sentences.en: Which color will they be repelled by?
sentences.zh: 哪种颜色会让他们感到排斥？

sentences.en: Clearly, the color stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 显然，这个颜色让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: I think I'm seeing it every time I see a green circle.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每次看到绿色圆圈我都会想到它。

sentences.en: So they presented children with several colors to choose from, and the consensus was that they liked the fluorescent green the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们向孩子们展示了几种颜色供选择，共识是他们最不喜欢荧光绿。

sentences.en: And while they did use a graphic designer to come up with the initial sketches, when it came to the final design, this is my favorite part,
sentences.zh: 虽然他们确实请了平面设计师来绘制草图，但在最终设计时，这是我最喜欢的部分，

sentences.en: they held a contest for kids via the Pittsburgh Poison Control Center.
sentences.zh: 他们通过匹兹堡毒物控制中心为孩子们举办了一场比赛。

sentences.en: And a fourth grader from West Virginia named Wendy Brown designed the logo and won the conteSt.
sentences.zh: 一位来自西弗吉尼亚州的四年级学生温迪·布朗设计了这个标志并赢得了比赛。

sentences.en: Oh, go for it, Wendy.
sentences.zh: 哦，加油，温迪。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: We tried to track her down for this story.
sentences.zh: 我们曾试图寻找她来讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: We could not find her, but Wendy, if you're listening, congratulations.
sentences.zh: 我们没能找到她，但温迪，如果你在听的话，恭喜你。

sentences.en: So they had the design and the color, but they still needed a catchy name.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有了设计和颜色，但还需要一个朗朗上口的名字。

sentences.en: We all know how important names are, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都知道名字有多重要，对吧？

sentences.en: So they went back to the kids and they showed them the sick face in fluorescent green.
sentences.zh: 于是他们回到孩子们身边，向他们展示了那个荧光绿色的痛苦表情。

sentences.en: And one kid said, he looks yucky.
sentences.zh: 有个孩子说，他看起来很讨厌（yucky）。

sentences.en: And that was a mic drop moment.
sentences.zh: 那一刻简直是神来之笔。

sentences.en: You got your name, Mr. Yuck.
sentences.zh: 名字有了，就叫“讨厌先生”。

sentences.en: Out of the mouth of babes.
sentences.zh: 童言无忌。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: In the words of Dr. Moriarty, the skull and crossbones were designed by adults for adults.
sentences.zh: 用莫里亚蒂医生的话说，骷髅头和交叉骨是成年人为成年人设计的。

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck is actually the first symbol specifically designed for kids.
sentences.zh: “讨厌先生”实际上是第一个专门为孩子设计的标志。

sentences.en: I mean, creating a symbol for young children is really an interesting design challenge because
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为幼儿创造一个标志是一个非常有趣的设计挑战，因为

sentences.en: a good portion of your audience doesn't even know how to read.
sentences.zh: 你的受众中有很大一部分人甚至还不识字。

sentences.en: So it has to be something very literal, very memorable and very easy to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以它必须非常直观、令人难忘且易于理解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So how popular did the Mr. Yuck program end up getting?
sentences.zh: 那么“讨厌先生”项目最终有多受欢迎呢？

sentences.en: So the Pittsburgh Poison Center mailed many, many sheets of the stickers to households around
sentences.zh: 匹兹堡毒物中心向宾夕法尼亚州及其他地区的家庭邮寄了许多贴纸，

sentences.en: Pennsylvania and beyond, which definitely got the word out.
sentences.zh: 这确实起到了宣传作用。

sentences.en: But Mr. Yuck really took off in 1975 after a PSA ran during the 1975 Super Bowl.
sentences.zh: 但“讨厌先生”真正流行起来是在1975年超级碗期间播放了一则公益广告之后。

sentences.en: Home is full of lots of things that children shouldn't touch.
sentences.zh: 家里有很多孩子不该碰的东西。

sentences.en: Home is full of bad things that can hurt you very much.
sentences.zh: 家里有很多会让你受重伤的坏东西。

sentences.en: Now there's a man whose face is green that you ought to get to know.
sentences.zh: 现在有一个脸是绿色的人，你应该认识一下。

sentences.en: He'll warn you when danger's coming fast or slow.
sentences.zh: 当危险来临时，他会提醒你。

sentences.en: Get to know his face in every single place.
sentences.zh: 在每个地方都要认识他的脸。

sentences.en: Parents like my mom dutifully slapped them onto bottles, spray cans, medications, yada, yada, yada.
sentences.zh: 像我妈妈那样的家长尽职尽责地把它们贴在瓶子、喷雾罐、药物等等上面。

sentences.en: And for kids like myself, Mr. Yuck was a daily household presence.
sentences.zh: 对于像我这样的孩子来说，“讨厌先生”是家里每天都能见到的存在。

sentences.en: My mom even put one on our home phone.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈甚至在我们家的电话上贴了一个。

sentences.en: Well, she's contributing to the semiotic drift here, Gillian.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她这是在造成符号漂移，吉莉安。

sentences.en: No, no, this is actually encouraged by the Poison Control Center so that you would always have the number at hand at the ready.
sentences.zh: 不，不，这实际上是毒物控制中心鼓励的做法，这样你就能随时随地拿到号码。

sentences.en: She wasn't suggesting that the that the phone was poisonous and that you were going to eat it or something.
sentences.zh: 她并不是暗示电话有毒，你会把它吃掉之类的。

sentences.en: OK, she was worried about a lot of things in my childhood.
sentences.zh: 好吧，她在我童年时确实担心很多事情。

sentences.en: I don't think that was one of them.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得那是其中之一。

sentences.en: So usage of Mr. Yuck actually did spread slightly beyond Pittsburgh,
sentences.zh: 所以“讨厌先生”的使用确实稍微扩展到了匹兹堡之外，

sentences.en: but it never became the ubiquitous national symbol for poison control centers.
sentences.zh: 但它从未成为全国毒物控制中心通用的标志。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是为什么？

sentences.en: I think one part of it was that initially Dr. Moriarty would only send the stickers to hospitals
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因是，最初莫里亚蒂医生只把贴纸发给那些

sentences.en: who agreed to participate in his Pittsburgh Poison Center program.
sentences.zh: 同意参与他匹兹堡毒物中心项目的医院。

sentences.en: And this required that the Pittsburgh Poison Center would be the central hub
sentences.zh: 这要求匹兹堡毒物中心作为中央枢纽，

sentences.en: and all the other centers would have to report back to them.

sentences.en: So, as you can see, this disjointed, uncoordinated approach meant Mr. Yuck wasn't as recognized in most parts of the U.S.

sentences.en: And this war of the poison control mascots kind of illustrated the problem with poison control centers across the country at the time
sentences.zh: 而这场毒物控制吉祥物之战，在某种程度上说明了当时全国毒物控制中心存在的问题，

sentences.en: because there still was no single coordinated poison control agency.
sentences.zh: 因为当时仍然没有一个统一协调的毒物控制机构。

sentences.en: So then what happened to Mr. Yuck?
sentences.zh: 那么后来“Yuck先生”怎么样了？

sentences.en: By the 1980s and 90s, the number of poison control centers started to decline.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪80年代和90年代，毒物控制中心的数量开始减少。

sentences.en: And then, in the early 2000s, Congress passed the Poison Control Center Enhancement and Awareness Act, which allocated support to poison centers.
sentences.zh: 然后，在21世纪初，国会通过了《毒物控制中心增强与意识法案》，为毒物中心提供了支持。

sentences.en: So now, 100% of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，100%的美国

sentences.en: population is served by just a single toll-free phone number from anywhere in the country.
sentences.zh: 人口都可以通过全国任何地方的同一个免费电话号码获得服务。

sentences.en: Which is great, but it also means that Mr. Yuck wasn't relevant anymore because people didn't need to be directed to the Pittsburgh Poison Center's number.

sentences.en: So basically, because we have one single national poison control number, Mr. Yuck just wasn't really useful anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，因为我们有了一个全国统一的毒物控制号码，“Yuck先生”就不再那么有用了。

sentences.en: Exactly.

sentences.zh: 匹兹堡毒物中心确实还在分发贴纸作为娱乐，但它们现在印的是全国毒物控制号码，即1-800-222-1222。

sentences.en: Oh, I'll also side note that when the national number was established, there was a push to adopt Mr. Yuck as the national symbol, but it was rejected in favor of, do you know,
sentences.zh: 哦，我还要顺便提一下，当全国号码建立时，曾有人推动将“Yuck先生”作为全国标志，但被拒绝了，转而选择了，你知道吗，

sentences.en: Roman?

sentences.en: I mean, well, the problem with skull and crossbones is it is iconic, but it's iconic for a lot of different reasons.
sentences.zh: 我是说，好吧，骷髅和交叉骨的问题在于它确实具有标志性，但它代表的含义太多了。

sentences.en: Like, it's cool looking.
sentences.zh: 比如，它看起来很酷。

sentences.en: It's, like, cool for pirates, you know.
sentences.zh: 比如，对海盗来说很酷，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's just not all poison anymore.
sentences.zh: 它不再仅仅代表毒药了。

sentences.en: But I guess what I'm curious about is if the Mr. Yuck branding really worked.
sentences.zh: 但我好奇的是，“Yuck先生”的品牌推广是否真的奏效了。

sentences.en: Like, did it actually reduce childhood accidental poisonings in and around the Pittsburgh area, at least?
sentences.zh: 比如，它是否真的减少了匹兹堡及其周边地区儿童意外中毒的事件？

sentences.en: So, Mr. Yuck launched in 1971, and within just a couple of years, rates of childhood poisoning actually began plummeting.
sentences.zh: “Yuck先生”于1971年推出，仅仅几年内，儿童中毒率确实开始大幅下降。

sentences.en: Wow, really?
sentences.zh: 哇，真的吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, but not because of Mr. Yuck.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这并不是因为“Yuck先生”。

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck is great for educational purposes and awareness, but you really need to prevent the kid who's really determined to get into that bottle.
sentences.zh: “Yuck先生”在教育和提高意识方面很棒，但你真的需要阻止那些决心要打开瓶子的孩子。

sentences.en: I mean, a three-year-old or a four-year-old has little impulse control and a lot of curiosity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，三四岁的孩子几乎没有冲动控制力，却有强烈的好奇心。

sentences.en: And so I've had one three-year-old, a four-year-old before, and so I know this.
sentences.zh: 我以前带过三四岁的孩子，所以我知道这一点。

sentences.en: They may not be deterred by any kind of, you know, symbol.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不会被任何种类的符号所震慑。

sentences.en: They're deterred by, you know, packaging that prevents them from getting into the actual package.
sentences.zh: 他们会被那种能防止他们打开包装的包装所阻挡。

sentences.en: That was Dr. Moser-Jones again.
sentences.zh: 那是莫泽-琼斯博士再次强调的。

sentences.en: And she says that in 1970, Congress passed the Poison Prevention Packaging Act, which mandated child-resistant packaging.
sentences.zh: 她说，1970年，国会通过了《毒物预防包装法案》，强制要求使用儿童安全包装。

sentences.en: In the intervening years, child-poisoning deaths have fallen by roughly 73%, and they have stayed low ever since.
sentences.zh: 在此后的几年里，儿童中毒死亡人数下降了约73%，并且一直保持在低位。

sentences.en: By 1981, childhood-poisoning death rates had fallen to 25% of their 1961 levels.
sentences.zh: 到1981年，儿童中毒死亡率已降至1961年水平的25%。

sentences.en: And since 1972, childhood-poisoning death rates have not gone back up.
sentences.zh: 自1972年以来，儿童中毒死亡率再也没有回升。

sentences.en: So this has saved lives, this kind of packaging and this enforcement, although some people may criticize it as being the nanny state.
sentences.zh: 所以这种包装和执法确实挽救了生命，尽管有些人可能会批评这是“保姆国家”。

sentences.en: It has saved lives.
sentences.zh: 它确实挽救了生命。

sentences.en: I mean, children need a nanny, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，孩子们确实需要保姆，对吧？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实需要。

sentences.en: They totally do.
sentences.zh: 完全需要。

sentences.en: This is not an example of the nanny state.
sentences.zh: 这并不是“保姆国家”的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, this is huge.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这意义重大。

sentences.en: Better packaging, better public awareness, quality access to poison control centers combined to, like, reduce a number in an extremely meaningful way.
sentences.zh: 更好的包装、更好的公众意识、高质量的毒物控制中心接入，共同以一种极其有效的方式降低了数字。

sentences.en: They stop these kids from getting sick or dying from household poisons.
sentences.zh: 它们阻止了这些孩子因家庭毒物而生病或死亡。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Yes, and I also have to mention that some have questioned the effectiveness of Mr. Yuck.
sentences.zh: 是的，我还必须提到，有些人质疑“Yuck先生”的有效性。

sentences.en: Some studies found that the symbol didn't deter children.
sentences.zh: 一些研究发现，这个符号并没有震慑住孩子。

sentences.en: And, in fact, some kids were actually drawn to ingesting harmful substances because of Mr. Yuck.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些孩子反而因为“Yuck先生”而被吸引去摄入有害物质。

sentences.en: What's funny is that I do remember the Mr. Yuck stickers.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我确实记得“Yuck先生”的贴纸。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Moser-Jones actually grew up with Mr. Yuck as a kid in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 莫泽-琼斯博士小时候就是在圣路易斯伴随着“Yuck先生”长大的。

sentences.en: The thing that stuck with me most was that in our basement, my mother had this old bottle.
sentences.zh: 最让我印象深刻的是，我母亲在地下室里有一个旧瓶子。

sentences.en: It was actually a jug with a skull and crossbones on it.
sentences.zh: 那其实是一个上面印有骷髅和交叉骨的罐子。

sentences.en: And that was much more impactful than Mr. Yuck stickers.
sentences.zh: 那比“Yuck先生”的贴纸更有冲击力。

sentences.en: And, again, I mean, I grew up in a time where there were these characters like Oscar the Grouch in Sesame Street who was sort of a yucky character.
sentences.zh: 而且，我是在那个时代长大的，当时《芝麻街》里有像“奥斯卡”这样有点讨厌的角色。

sentences.en: I mean, he lived in the trash.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他住在垃圾桶里。

sentences.en: He sang these songs about being dirty.
sentences.zh: 他唱着关于自己很脏的歌。

sentences.en: And so they were kind of these kind of dirty and, you know, yucky characters were somewhat appealing.
sentences.zh: 所以那些脏兮兮的、令人讨厌的角色在某种程度上是有吸引力的。

sentences.en: And so I do think that there is a problem when you have a sticker that could be appealing to kids as well and not just scary.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，当你有一个可能对孩子有吸引力而不仅仅是可怕的贴纸时，就会出现问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a problem for all symbols.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这对所有符号来说都是一个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, just like, you know, kids and people just have their own opinions about what a symbol means.
sentences.zh: 我是说，就像孩子们和人们对一个符号的含义有自己的看法一样。

sentences.en: And it always shifts.

sentences.en: I don't want to sell Mr. Yuck short at all.

sentences.en: I love the guy.
sentences.zh: 我爱这个家伙。

sentences.en: You know, it was a campaign that spread a lot of important awareness about the poison control system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一场传播了大量关于毒物控制系统重要意识的运动。

sentences.en: So Mr. Yuck may not have been the hero of the poison control movement, but he was definitely a hero in Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 所以“Yuck先生”可能不是毒物控制运动的英雄，但他绝对是匹兹堡的英雄。

sentences.zh: 假设一名工人在使用该工具时戴着防护手套，那么这些手套很可能也是放射性的。

sentences.en: The Waste Isolation Pilot Plant was designed to store all of this stuff and keep us all safe from it.
sentences.zh: “废物隔离试验工厂”的设计初衷就是为了储存所有这些东西，并保护我们免受其害。

sentences.en: The WIPP site is in New Mexico, deep in the desert, about 26 miles east of Carlsbad.
sentences.zh: WIPP现场位于新墨西哥州，深处沙漠，在卡尔斯巴德以东约26英里处。

sentences.en: It's a really cool place.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常酷的地方。

sentences.en: It reminded me of kind of the headquarters of Spectre or Dr. No in a James Bond novel.
sentences.zh: 它让我想起了詹姆斯·邦德小说中“幽灵党”或“诺博士”的总部。

sentences.en: John saw the WIPP site in person when he accepted the invitation from Sandia Labs to go be a part of their big groupthink on designing a 10,000-year warning for the place.
sentences.zh: 约翰在接受桑迪亚实验室的邀请，去参加他们关于为该地点设计1万年警告的大型集体讨论时，亲眼看到了WIPP现场。

sentences.en: How could you turn it down?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能拒绝呢？

sentences.en: This was in 1991.
sentences.zh: 那是在1991年。

sentences.en: So the workers took John into an elevator shaft.
sentences.zh: 所以工人们带着约翰进入了一个电梯井。

sentences.en: And they go down about half a mile beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 他们下到了地表以下约半英里处。

sentences.en: And that's where John saw these enormous caverns.
sentences.zh: 就在那里，约翰看到了这些巨大的洞穴。

sentences.en: They've carved out this repository in basically a salt deposit.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在一个盐矿床里开凿出了这个储存库。

sentences.en: Salt deposit, 200 million years old.
sentences.zh: 盐矿床，已有两亿年的历史。

sentences.en: And, you know, we think of salt as white, but this salt, for reasons I don't understand, was kind of a salmon-y pink color.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们通常认为盐是白色的，但这种盐，出于我不理解的原因，呈现出一种类似三文鱼的粉红色。

sentences.en: So the walls of this place were all crystalline with this sort of shot through with these hues of salmon and pink and orange.
sentences.zh: 所以这个地方的墙壁全是结晶体，透着一种三文鱼色、粉色和橙色的色调。

sentences.en: So it was actually quite beautiful.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上非常漂亮。

sentences.en: All this radioactive stuff will all be loaded into thousands of oil drums and packed into these caverns.
sentences.zh: 所有这些放射性物质都将被装进数千个油桶，并塞进这些洞穴里。

sentences.en: And then this underground chamber will be sealed up and left alone.
sentences.zh: 然后这个地下室将被密封起来，不再有人打扰。

sentences.en: Years will pass, and those years will become decades.
sentences.zh: 岁月流逝，这些年头将变成几十年。

sentences.en: And those decades will become centuries.
sentences.zh: 而这几十年将变成几个世纪。

sentences.en: And centuries will roll into millennia.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪将汇聚成几千年。

sentences.en: And people above ground will come and go.
sentences.zh: 地面上的人们来来去去。

sentences.en: Cultures will rise and fall.
sentences.zh: 文明兴起又衰落。

sentences.en: And all the while, below the surface, the salt will do what salt does with the right temperature and pressure.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，在地表之下，盐会在合适的温度和压力下做它该做的事。

sentences.en: It will slowly creep, making that cave full of waste smaller and smaller and smaller.
sentences.zh: 它会缓慢地蠕动，让那个装满废料的洞穴变得越来越小。

sentences.en: Until the salt swallows up all those oil drums, crushing them.
sentences.zh: 直到盐吞没所有那些油桶，将它们压碎。

sentences.en: Entombing them.
sentences.zh: 将它们埋葬。

sentences.en: And so there, solidified in the Earth's crust, will be these gloves and these tools and these little bits from bombs that we made.
sentences.zh: 于是，凝固在地壳中的，将是我们制造的炸弹留下的手套、工具和碎片。

sentences.en: All still radioactive.
sentences.zh: 依然具有放射性。

sentences.en: Poisonous.
sentences.zh: 有毒。

sentences.en: For more than 200,000 years.
sentences.zh: 持续超过二十万年。

sentences.en: Basically forever.
sentences.zh: 基本上是永远。

sentences.en: Storing something dangerous safely forever is a huge design problem.
sentences.zh: 如何安全地永久储存危险品是一个巨大的设计难题。

sentences.en: In fact, the jury is still out on whether they saw the basics of the storage problem at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于他们是否真正看清了储存问题的本质，目前尚无定论。

sentences.en: In February of 2014, a leak was detected that exposed several workers to low levels of radiation, and WIP has been closed since.
sentences.zh: 2014年2月，检测到一次泄漏，导致几名工人受到低剂量辐射，WIP（废料隔离试验工厂）自此关闭。

sentences.en: The Department of Energy now predicts that it could be up to three years before WIP is fully operational again.
sentences.zh: 能源部现在预测，WIP可能需要长达三年时间才能完全恢复运作。

sentences.en: We know these facts because we can look it up and read the news in a shared language.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这些事实，因为我们可以通过共享的语言查阅和阅读新闻。

sentences.en: But the problem that John Lomberg was brought out to New Mexico to solve was not about communicating the danger of WIP to people today.
sentences.zh: 但约翰·隆伯格（John Lomberg）被请到新墨西哥州要解决的问题，并不是如何向今天的人们传达WIP的危险性。

sentences.en: He wanted to figure out how to tell people millennia from now that this place is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 他想弄清楚如何告诉几千年后的人们，这个地方很危险。

sentences.en: When John Lomberg arrived in New Mexico, he met the teammates he'd be collaborating with.
sentences.zh: 当约翰·隆伯格到达新墨西哥州时，他见到了将与他合作的团队成员。

sentences.en: There were geologists, linguists, astrophysicists.
sentences.zh: 有地质学家、语言学家、天体物理学家。

sentences.en: There was science fiction writer Gregory Benford.
sentences.zh: 还有科幻作家格雷戈里·本福德（Gregory Benford）。

sentences.en: And he would be the archaeologiSt.
sentences.zh: 而他将担任考古学家。

sentences.en: This is Maureen.
sentences.zh: 这位是莫琳（Maureen）。

sentences.en: Maureen Kaplan.
sentences.zh: 莫琳·卡普兰（Maureen Kaplan）。

sentences.en: An archaeologist with a consulting firm ERG.
sentences.zh: 咨询公司ERG的一位考古学家。

sentences.en: Do you remember what you thought of the people they'd gotten together, like when you first saw them?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你对他们召集来的这些人有什么看法吗，比如你第一次见到他们的时候？

sentences.en: Um, it was like, oh my goodness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时的感觉是，哦，天哪。

sentences.en: She was kind of starstruck.
sentences.zh: 她当时有点被明星光环震住了。

sentences.en: I went, John Lomberg, wait a moment.
sentences.zh: 我说，约翰·隆伯格，等一下。

sentences.en: Aren't you the one who did the picture that went off into space in terms of trying to communicate with whoever might find Voyager?
sentences.zh: 你不是那个制作了那张飞向太空的图片的人吗，就是为了尝试与任何可能发现旅行者号的外星生命交流？

sentences.en: So I was impressed.
sentences.zh: 所以我印象很深。

sentences.en: After hellos and whatnot, the Sandia folks split all these Smarties into two different groups.
sentences.zh: 寒暄过后，桑迪亚（Sandia）实验室的人把这些聪明人分成了两组。

sentences.en: So they'd have kind of two separate thinking processes.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就有两种独立的思维过程。

sentences.en: John was in group B, Maureen group A.
sentences.zh: 约翰在B组，莫琳在A组。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: And then they laid down the ground rules.
sentences.zh: 然后他们制定了基本规则。

sentences.en: They told us to assume that we're designing a warning marker for humans.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们要假设我们是在为人类设计一个警告标志。

sentences.en: Not aliens, not cyborgs.
sentences.zh: 不是外星人，也不是半机械人。

sentences.en: But for a human being biologically identical to us, but who's alive 500 or 5,000 or 10,000 years from now.
sentences.zh: 而是为生理上与我们完全相同，但生活在500年、5000年或10000年后的人类。

sentences.en: How can you make a message that that human will understand?
sentences.zh: 你怎样才能制作出那个人类能理解的信息？

sentences.en: And why 10,000 years?
sentences.zh: 为什么是10000年？

sentences.en: As far as I could determine, the logic seemed to be, well, if we told them to design a marker to last 250,000 years, that's clearly a ridiculous and absurd proposition.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，逻辑似乎是，好吧，如果我们让他们设计一个能持续25万年的标志，那显然是一个荒谬可笑的提议。

sentences.en: 10,000 years doesn't sound quite so crazy.
sentences.zh: 10000年听起来没那么疯狂。

sentences.en: So it was just pulled out of the air.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是随口一说。

sentences.en: In other words, even though this site is going to be radioactive for hundreds of thousands of years,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，尽管这个地点在几十万年内都将具有放射性，

sentences.en: this panel was only responsible for keeping this place sufficiently labeled for humans for the next 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 但这个小组只负责在未来10000年内为人类充分标记好这个地方。

sentences.en: Let's get some perspective.
sentences.zh: 让我们换个角度看看。

sentences.en: Think about where humanity was 10,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 想想10000年前人类处于什么水平。

sentences.en: Back then, there was a hot new technology taking the world by storm.
sentences.zh: 那时，一项风靡全球的热门新技术刚刚出现。

sentences.en: It was called farming.
sentences.zh: 它叫农业。

sentences.en: Before the agricultural revolution, humans subsisted as gatherer hunters.
sentences.zh: 在农业革命之前，人类以狩猎采集为生。

sentences.en: Biologically, we are the same people we were 10,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 从生理上讲，我们和10000年前的人是一样的。

sentences.en: Actually, that's true going back over 40,000 years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，追溯到40000多年前也是如此。

sentences.en: But culturally, we share almost nothing with these people.
sentences.zh: 但在文化上，我们与这些人几乎没有任何共同之处。

sentences.en: Definitely not language.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有共同语言。

sentences.en: Well, no, because the linguists tell us that language changes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，因为语言学家告诉我们语言是会变的。

sentences.en: Language has a half-life, just like radioactive materials have a half-life.
sentences.zh: 语言有半衰期，就像放射性物质有半衰期一样。

sentences.en: And this half-life isn't very long.
sentences.zh: 而且这个半衰期并不长。

sentences.en: Think about Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 想想莎士比亚。

sentences.en: My cousin Westmoreland, nay, my fair cousin.
sentences.zh: 我的威斯特摩兰表弟，不，我亲爱的表弟。

sentences.en: Alack, what poverty my muse brings forth.
sentences.zh: 唉，我的缪斯带来了多么贫乏的诗句。

sentences.en: But this dotage of our generals o'er flows the measure.
sentences.zh: 但我们将军们的这种痴迷已经过分了。

sentences.en: Some of the words are tough.
sentences.zh: 有些词很难懂。

sentences.en: Bully rook.
sentences.zh: Bully rook（恶棍）。

sentences.en: Festinately.
sentences.zh: Festinately（匆忙地）。

sentences.en: Fleshment.
sentences.zh: Fleshment（初战告捷）。

sentences.en: Clinquant.
sentences.zh: Clinquant（闪闪发光的）。

sentences.en: Is that how you say that?
sentences.zh: 是这样读的吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, high schoolers can get through it.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，高中生还是能读懂的。

sentences.en: Although Shakespeare was only 400 years ago.
sentences.zh: 尽管莎士比亚距今只有400年。

sentences.en: 4% of 10,000 years.
What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Go back to Beowulf?
sentences.zh: 回到《贝奥武夫》？

sentences.en: Way gardener.
sentences.zh: Way gardener（守卫者）。

sentences.en: Written in Old English?
sentences.zh: 用古英语写的？

sentences.en: Theod König a thrym je frunon.
sentences.zh: Theod König a thrym je frunon（我们听闻了国王的威严）。

sentences.en: Basically incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 基本上无法理解。

sentences.en: El en fremedon.
sentences.zh: El en fremedon（他们做出的英勇事迹）。

sentences.en: Oft shul shavings sherzen a threatum.
sentences.zh: Oft shul shavings sherzen a threatum（经常在威胁中……）。

sentences.en: And it's like a different language.
sentences.zh: 这就像是另一种语言。

sentences.en: And I know you can't see this because this is radio, but trust me, it's just as confusing on the written page.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们看不见，因为这是广播，但相信我，写在纸上同样令人困惑。

sentences.en: You can recognize most of the letters as being part of the English alphabet, but they barely correspond with how we use those letters today.
sentences.zh: 你能认出大部分字母是英文字母的一部分，但它们与我们今天使用这些字母的方式几乎没有对应关系。

sentences.en: And that's from year 1,000, 10% of 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 而那还是1000年前的事，仅占10000年的10%。

sentences.en: There are some languages that are very resistant to change.
sentences.zh: 有些语言是非常抗拒变化的。

sentences.en: That is languages that get enshrined in biblical texts, in religious texts.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些被铭刻在圣经文本、宗教文本中的语言。

sentences.en: Latin, Hebrew, Arabic.
sentences.zh: 拉丁语、希伯来语、阿拉伯语。

sentences.en: But those aren't sure bets either.
sentences.zh: 但这些也不是万无一失的。

sentences.en: The oldest written texts go back to ancient Samaria, about 4,600 years ago.
sentences.zh: 最早的书面文本可以追溯到大约4600年前的古苏美尔。

sentences.en: And those languages are long since dead.
sentences.zh: 而那些语言早已消亡。

sentences.en: And that's not even the halfway mark of our time frame.
sentences.zh: 那甚至还不到我们时间跨度的一半。

sentences.en: So, both Team A and Team B at the WIP brainstorming session realized pretty quickly that every language on the planet today could be gone well before 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 所以，WIP头脑风暴会议上的A组和B组很快意识到，今天地球上的每一种语言在10000年之前可能就消失了。

sentences.en: And how can you start a conversation with somebody that you have no common language with?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何与一个没有任何共同语言的人开始对话呢？

sentences.en: Both groups weren't sure about this.
sentences.zh: 两组人对此都没有把握。

sentences.en: But then they thought, there's got to be something better than language.
sentences.zh: 但后来他们想，一定有比语言更好的东西。

sentences.en: Symbols.
sentences.zh: 符号。

sentences.en: Symbols.
sentences.zh: 符号。

sentences.en: There are some facial expressions which are pretty universal.
sentences.zh: 有些面部表情是非常通用的。

sentences.en: Like, the smiley face.
sentences.zh: 比如，笑脸。

sentences.en: Two dots for eyes, half circle for a mouth.
sentences.zh: 两个点作为眼睛，半圆作为嘴巴。

sentences.en: It's happy.
sentences.zh: 它代表快乐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And take another one.
sentences.zh: 再看另一个。

sentences.en: For like, yuck.
sentences.zh: 比如，厌恶。

sentences.en: Symbol called Mr. Yuck.
sentences.zh: 叫“厌恶先生”（Mr. Yuck）的符号。

sentences.en: If you were alive in the 80s, you know this one.
sentences.zh: 如果你生活在80年代，你就知道这个。

sentences.en: Yuck is mean.
sentences.zh: 厌恶是刻薄的。

sentences.en: Mr. Yuck is green.
sentences.zh: 厌恶先生是绿色的。

sentences.en: It's a logo of a green face with squinty eyes and a stuck-out tongue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绿色脸孔的标志，眯着眼睛，伸着舌头。

sentences.en: The face looks like it's about to be sick.
sentences.zh: 那张脸看起来好像快要吐了。

sentences.en: Sick, sick, sick.
sentences.zh: 恶心，恶心，恶心。

sentences.en: It was designed to be put on cleaning products and other household poisons to let kids know that whatever's inside is going to be horrible for you.
sentences.zh: 它被设计用来贴在清洁产品和其他家用毒物上，让孩子们知道里面的东西对身体有害。

sentences.en: And so, thinking along those lines, they considered another logo, which they thought might be universal.
sentences.zh: 因此，沿着这个思路，他们考虑了另一个他们认为可能是通用的标志。

sentences.en: Actually, Carl Sagan proposed it.
sentences.zh: 实际上，卡尔·萨根（Carl Sagan）提议过。

sentences.en: Sagan couldn't make the panel, but he sent in a letter saying this whole marker problem was easy.
sentences.zh: 萨根没能参加会议，但他寄来一封信说，这个标志问题很简单。

sentences.en: You just need the right symbol.
sentences.zh: 你只需要正确的符号。

sentences.en: And he knew just the one.
sentences.zh: 而且他知道选哪一个。

sentences.en: The skull and crossbones.
sentences.zh: 骷髅头和交叉骨。

sentences.en: They're Jolly Roger.
sentences.zh: 也就是海盗旗。

sentences.en: Death incarnate.
sentences.zh: 死亡的化身。

sentences.en: Well, do you know where the skull and crossbones came from?
sentences.zh: 那么，你知道骷髅头和交叉骨是从哪里来的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不知道。

sentences.en: The earliest uses of it are in religious paintings and sculptures from the Middle Ages, where at the foot of the cross, where Jesus is crucified,
sentences.zh: 它最早出现在中世纪的宗教绘画和雕塑中，在耶稣受难的十字架脚下，

sentences.en: there's a skull with two bones in the shape of a cross.
sentences.zh: 有一个骷髅和两根骨头组成的十字形状。

sentences.en: Not an X, the shape of a cross.
sentences.zh: 不是X形，是十字形。

sentences.en: And it's Adam's skull.
sentences.zh: 那是亚当的头骨。

sentences.en: And the bones are the symbol of the resurrection.
sentences.zh: 而骨头是复活的象征。

sentences.en: So, instead of it being a symbol of death, it was a symbol of resurrection and rebirth.
sentences.zh: 所以，它最初不是死亡的象征，而是复活和重生的象征。

sentences.en: But, fast forward a couple of centuries.
sentences.zh: 但是，快进几个世纪。

sentences.en: There's a lot of trade going on, merchant ships traveling to and fro.
sentences.zh: 贸易往来频繁，商船来来往往。

sentences.en: And in the ship's log, if a sailor died, the captain would put a little skull and crossbones next to his name.
sentences.zh: 在航海日志里，如果水手死了，船长会在他的名字旁边画一个小骷髅头和交叉骨。

sentences.en: And a lot of the sailors came to associate that symbol with death.
sentences.zh: 很多水手开始把那个符号与死亡联系起来。

sentences.en: The rebirth part of it was kind of loSt.
sentences.zh: 重生的那部分含义被遗忘了。

sentences.en: Fast forward another century.
sentences.zh: 再快进一个世纪。

sentences.en: You've got pirates out marauding on the high seas.
sentences.zh: 海盗在公海上掠夺。

sentences.en: They've plundered other boats and stole their cargo.
sentences.zh: 他们洗劫其他船只，偷走货物。

sentences.en: And along the way, some pirates realized they could use a symbol to let their targets know who they were.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，一些海盗意识到他们可以使用一个符号来让目标知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: A branding campaign to terrify their targets into compliance.
sentences.zh: 一种通过恐吓目标使其屈服的品牌宣传活动。

sentences.en: Yeah, to make clear, we're pirates.
sentences.zh: 没错，为了明确表示：我们是海盗。

sentences.en: And if you don't surrender, we're going to kill you.
sentences.zh: 如果你不投降，我们就杀了你。

sentences.en: It's your death.
sentences.zh: 那是你的死期。

sentences.en: But there were actually several different icons that pirates used.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，海盗们使用过好几种不同的图标。

sentences.en: For example, a heart with blood dripping out of it.
sentences.zh: 比如，一颗滴着血的心脏。

sentences.en: That was a popular pirate flag?
sentences.zh: 那曾是一种流行的海盗旗吗？

sentences.en: And an even more popular symbol was an hourglass.
sentences.zh: 而另一种更流行的符号是沙漏。

sentences.en: An hourglass.
sentences.zh: 沙漏。

sentences.en: An hourglass meant, if you don't surrender in a certain amount of time, we're going to kill you all.
sentences.zh: 沙漏的意思是：如果你不在一定时间内投降，我们就会把你们全部杀光。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: So the hourglass for a while was the most feared pirate symbol.
sentences.zh: 所以有一段时间，沙漏是海盗最令人恐惧的标志。

sentences.en: But then one of the logos got famous.
sentences.zh: 但后来，其中一个标志变得出名了。

sentences.en: In 1720, a pirate named Calico Jack Rackham was captured and put on trial.
sentences.zh: 1720年，一名叫“棉布杰克”雷克汉姆的海盗被捕并受审。

sentences.en: In the legal proceedings, it came out that two of the pirates in Calico Jack's crew were women.
sentences.zh: 在法律诉讼过程中，人们发现“棉布杰克”船上的两名海盗竟然是女性。

sentences.en: And that one of them was pregnant with Calico Jack's child.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一人还怀着“棉布杰克”的孩子。

sentences.en: This was the tabloid scandal of the day.
sentences.zh: 这可是当时轰动一时的丑闻。

sentences.en: And everyone in England was reading about this trial.
sentences.zh: 全英国的人都在读关于这场审判的报道。

sentences.en: Anyway, it just so happened that Calico Jack's symbol was the Jolly Roger.
sentences.zh: 总之，碰巧“棉布杰克”的标志就是“海盗旗”（Jolly Roger）。

sentences.en: Though, in his case, the bones were replaced with a pair of cross swords.
sentences.zh: 不过，他的旗帜上，骨头被换成了一对交叉的剑。

sentences.en: Quick aside.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下。

sentences.en: The name Jolly Roger is probably an English corruption of the French Jolie Rouge, or pretty red.
sentences.zh: “Jolly Roger”这个名字很可能是法语“Jolie Rouge”（漂亮的红色）的英语讹传。

sentences.en: Because the original pirate flags were red, not black.
sentences.zh: 因为最初的海盗旗是红色的，而不是黑色的。

sentences.en: After that trial, the skull and crossbones started showing up on book covers.
sentences.zh: 那场审判之后，骷髅交叉骨的图案开始出现在书封上。

sentences.en: Treasure Island kind of novels.
sentences.zh: 比如《金银岛》这类小说。

sentences.en: The skull and crossbones was permeating culture as a symbol of danger.
sentences.zh: 骷髅交叉骨作为危险的象征，开始渗透到文化中。

sentences.en: Jump ahead to the late 1800s.
sentences.zh: 快进到19世纪末。

sentences.en: Dye factories in Germany started using the skull and crossbones as a symbol for poison.
sentences.zh: 德国的染料工厂开始使用骷髅交叉骨作为剧毒的标志。

sentences.en: Half a century later.
sentences.zh: 半个世纪后。

sentences.en: The Nazis adopted it as the symbol for their SS death's head divisions.
sentences.zh: 纳粹将其采纳为党卫队骷髅总队的标志。

sentences.en: So the skull and crossbones came to be associated with danger and death around the world.
sentences.zh: 于是，骷髅交叉骨在世界范围内与危险和死亡联系在了一起。

sentences.en: But it didn't become universal.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有成为通用的标志。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并不完全是。

sentences.en: Think about what's happened with the skull and crossbones in the last 20, 30 years.
sentences.zh: 想想过去二三十年里骷髅交叉骨发生了什么变化。

sentences.en: It's gone mainstream.
sentences.zh: 它已经成为主流了。

sentences.en: Now you'll see it on kids' book bags, on onesies for infants.
sentences.zh: 现在你会在孩子的书包上、婴儿的连体衣上看到它。

sentences.en: You can even buy water bottles with the skull and crossbones.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以买到印有骷髅交叉骨的水瓶。

sentences.en: So much for the whole poison thing.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“剧毒”含义也就到此为止了。

sentences.en: And the original meaning as it pertained to Adam and the resurrection is long gone.
sentences.zh: 而它最初与亚当和复活相关的含义早已消失殆尽。

sentences.en: The lesson that we took from this is that symbols can change.
sentences.zh: 我们从中得到的教训是，符号是可以改变的。

sentences.en: Iconographical drift happens.
sentences.zh: 图标含义的漂移是会发生的。

sentences.en: And we haven't even touched on cultural interpretation.
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至还没触及文化解读层面。

sentences.en: Like there's a candy company in Mexico called La Catrina.
sentences.zh: 比如墨西哥有一家叫“La Catrina”的糖果公司。

sentences.en: And their logo, the logo that goes on the packaging for their sweets, is a skull.
sentences.zh: 他们的标志，也就是印在糖果包装上的那个标志，就是一个骷髅头。

sentences.en: And so to bring us back to the WIPP site in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们回到新墨西哥州的WIPP（核废料隔离试验工厂）选址。

sentences.en: The two teams of smart people at WIPP realized that symbols couldn't be trusted to mean the same things over time.
sentences.zh: WIPP的两支专家团队意识到，不能指望符号在漫长的时间里保持相同的含义。

sentences.en: So next idea.
sentences.zh: 所以，下一个主意。

sentences.en: We could tell a little story using stick figures.
sentences.zh: 我们可以用火柴人讲一个小故事。

sentences.en: Visual storytelling.
sentences.zh: 视觉叙事。

sentences.en: A stick figure that like any five-year-old could draw.
sentences.zh: 一个任何五岁小孩都能画出来的火柴人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Circle on top, a trunk, two arms and two legs.
sentences.zh: 上面画个圆，中间画个躯干，再画两条胳膊和两条腿。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, there are two things that seem to be universal in human art.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人类艺术中有两样东西似乎是通用的。

sentences.en: One is a stick figure.
sentences.zh: 一个是火柴人。

sentences.en: And you find them all drawn on the walls of the caves and the cave paintings that are 25,000 years old.
sentences.zh: 你在两万五千年前的洞穴壁画上都能找到它们。

sentences.en: Which, by the way, may be the only piece of graphic art surviving for more than 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这可能是唯一能留存超过一万年的图形艺术作品。

sentences.en: That is art from which we can draw meaning.
sentences.zh: 那是我们能够从中解读出意义的艺术。

sentences.en: And John says there's another convention that is universal.
sentences.zh: 约翰说还有另一种通用的惯例。

sentences.en: A sequence of events.
sentences.zh: 事件的先后顺序。

sentences.en: First this happened, then this happened, and then this happened.
sentences.zh: 先发生了这个，然后发生了那个，最后发生了那个。

sentences.en: So like a narrative, a story.
sentences.zh: 就像叙事，一个故事。

sentences.en: A narrative, a storyboard, a comic strip.
sentences.zh: 一种叙事、分镜脚本、连环画。

sentences.en: You just find it everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你到处都能见到它。

sentences.en: And in fact, you can even define a symbol using stick figures.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你甚至可以用火柴人来定义一个符号。

sentences.en: Check it out.
sentences.zh: 看看这个。

sentences.en: Let's do a simple comic strip.
sentences.zh: 我们来做一个简单的连环画。

sentences.en: So, first frame.
sentences.zh: 第一格。

sentences.en: You put a small child.
sentences.zh: 画一个小孩。

sentences.en: And the child is in front of a small plant, a sapling.
sentences.zh: 小孩站在一株小植物、一棵树苗前面。

sentences.en: Second frame.
sentences.zh: 第二格。

sentences.en: That child is a little bit bigger now.
sentences.zh: 那个孩子稍微长大了一点。

sentences.en: And the sapling behind him has grown a little bit.
sentences.zh: 他身后的树苗也长高了一些。

sentences.en: And next to the child is a barrel.
sentences.zh: 孩子旁边有一个桶。

sentences.en: And on that barrel is the symbol for radiation, the trefoil symbol.
sentences.zh: 桶上印着辐射标志，也就是那个三叶草符号。

sentences.en: And the child is touching that barrel.
sentences.zh: 孩子正在触摸那个桶。

sentences.en: Go to the third frame.
sentences.zh: 第三格。

sentences.en: You've got a full-grown big old tree.
sentences.zh: 你看到了一棵长成的大树。

sentences.en: You've got a child that is now an adult, a human being.
sentences.zh: 那个孩子现在已经长成了成年人。

sentences.en: Except the person is lying on the ground, presumably dead.
sentences.zh: 只不过这个人躺在地上，大概是死了。

sentences.en: X's over their eyes, frowny mouth.
sentences.zh: 眼睛画着叉，嘴巴向下撇。

sentences.en: And the barrel now with the trefoil symbol is open.
sentences.zh: 而那个印有三叶草符号的桶现在是打开的。

sentences.en: And so clearly, the idea is don't touch anything with the trefoil symbol.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，意思就是：不要碰任何带有三叶草符号的东西。

sentences.en: Or at least not a barrel.
sentences.zh: 或者至少不要碰那种桶。

sentences.en: Of course, if you read it from right to left, then it's a totally different story.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你从右往左读，那故事就完全变了。

sentences.en: The old guy who is sick discovers the fountain of youth.
sentences.zh: 那个生病的老人发现了长生不老泉。

sentences.en: And he's reborn.
sentences.zh: 然后他重生了。

sentences.en: Okay, all is not loSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，还没完全没救。

sentences.en: Maybe you could use arrows.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以用箭头。

sentences.en: Arrows are universal.
sentences.zh: 箭头是通用的。

sentences.en: Or maybe you could situate the various comic strips in a sequence
sentences.zh: 或者你可以把各种连环画按顺序排列，

sentences.en: that you can only see sequentially based on how they're arranged in the space.
sentences.zh: 让人们只能根据它们在空间中的排列顺序来依次观看。

sentences.en: So, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe it's possible to create a universally recognizable warning sign that way.
sentences.zh: 也许用这种方式创造一个全球通用的警告标志是可能的。

sentences.en: But really, regardless of whatever symbol we're trying to come up with
sentences.zh: 但说真的，无论我们试图想出什么样的符号，

sentences.en: or whatever story that we're trying to tell,
sentences.zh: 或者试图讲述什么样的故事，

sentences.en: can we actually build something, make something,
sentences.zh: 我们真的能建造出什么东西，制造出什么东西，

sentences.en: like a physical, tangible thing that can last 10,000 years?
sentences.zh: 比如一个能存在一万年的实体、有形的东西吗？

sentences.en: The brainstormers at WIPP thought about building something from solid gold.
sentences.zh: WIPP的头脑风暴小组曾考虑用纯金建造一些东西。

sentences.en: Well, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 嗯，结果会怎样呢？

sentences.en: They're going to get stolen.
sentences.zh: 它们会被偷走。

sentences.en: Maureen Kaplan, the archaeologist, her group realized the same thing.
sentences.zh: 考古学家莫琳·卡普兰和她的团队也意识到了同样的问题。

sentences.en: Medals were going to get recycled.
sentences.zh: 金属会被回收利用。

sentences.en: So, no bronze, no aluminum.
sentences.zh: 所以，不能用青铜，不能用铝。

sentences.en: That basically leaves you with rocks.
sentences.zh: 基本上只剩下石头了。

sentences.en: And rocks can erode.
sentences.zh: 但石头也会风化。

sentences.en: And who knows?
sentences.zh: 而且谁知道呢？

sentences.en: A giant monolith could be useful to some future desert person.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的巨石碑对未来的沙漠居民来说可能很有用。

sentences.en: You could, you know, just tip it over on its side and then you have a foundation for your house.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们可以把它推倒，然后作为房子的地基。

sentences.en: Here is the critical moment where all the obvious choices have been exhausted.
sentences.zh: 这是关键时刻，所有显而易见的选择都已耗尽。

sentences.en: Language, symbols, and storyboards weren't going to cut it.
sentences.zh: 语言、符号和分镜脚本都行不通。

sentences.en: And here's where plans for the WIPP site start getting really wacky.
sentences.zh: 而WIPP选址的计划也从这里开始变得非常古怪。

sentences.en: There was this one guy in Maureen's group named Mike Brill.
sentences.zh: 莫琳小组里有个叫迈克·布里尔的人。

sentences.en: Mike Brill was a landscape architect.
sentences.zh: 迈克·布里尔是一位景观设计师。

sentences.en: And an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 也是一位艺术家。

sentences.en: Brill has since passed away.
sentences.zh: 布里尔后来去世了。

sentences.en: But Maureen remembers in their group, Brill had this revelation.
sentences.zh: 但莫琳记得在他们小组里，布里尔有过这样一个启示。

sentences.en: You don't actually need to transmit information into the future.
sentences.zh: 你其实不需要向未来传递信息。

sentences.en: All you need to do is make somebody scared of being in that place.
sentences.zh: 你只需要让人们对身处那个地方感到恐惧就行了。

sentences.en: He was trying to sculpt the landscape such that it in itself gave a warning to people who were coming there.
sentences.zh: 他试图雕塑景观，使其本身就能给来到那里的人发出警告。

sentences.en: And he was thinking on a massive scale.
sentences.zh: 而且他的构思规模宏大。

sentences.en: On a scale greater than I'd ever imagined.
sentences.zh: 规模大到我从未想象过。

sentences.en: Like one drawing, which Mike called the Landscape of Thorns.
sentences.zh: 比如其中一个设计，迈克称之为“荆棘景观”。

sentences.en: A drawing of these huge needles.
sentences.zh: 画着这些巨大的针状物。

sentences.en: Sharp, pointed, angular.
sentences.zh: 尖锐、锋利、棱角分明。

sentences.en: Jutting up from the ground.
sentences.zh: 从地面突出来。

sentences.en: You know, the earth itself became a cactus.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大地本身变成了一株仙人掌。

sentences.en: Make the land itself ominous and impassable.
sentences.zh: 让这片土地本身变得不祥且无法通行。

sentences.en: But.
sentences.zh: 但是。

sentences.en: The last thing you want to do is draw people to see this incredible work of art.
sentences.zh: 你最不想做的事就是吸引人们来看这件不可思议的艺术品。

sentences.en: It's, you got to see this thing.
sentences.zh: “你一定要来看看这个东西。”

sentences.en: It's a half mile of these giant spikes.
sentences.zh: “这是半英里长的巨大尖刺。”

sentences.en: What the hell is it?
sentences.zh: “那到底是什么鬼东西？”

sentences.en: So, so somebody builds a hotel for them to stay in and they decide to dig a well for water.
sentences.zh: 于是，有人为他们建了旅馆，他们决定挖口井取水。

sentences.en: And there you are.
sentences.zh: 然后你就中招了。

sentences.en: You've just caused exactly what you're trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 你正好造成了你试图避免的结果。

sentences.en: When all was said and done, both groups submitted their proposals.
sentences.zh: 最终，两个小组都提交了他们的提案。

sentences.en: But Sandia Labs found most of the ideas a little too pie in the sky.
sentences.zh: 但桑迪亚国家实验室认为大多数想法太不切实际了。

sentences.en: Here's Roger Nelson, the chief scientist at the Department of Energy's Carlsbad Field Office, which owns and operates WIP.
sentences.zh: 这位是罗杰·尼尔森，能源部卡尔斯巴德现场办公室的首席科学家，该办公室拥有并运营WIPP。

sentences.en: If we build any markers,
sentences.zh: 如果我们建造任何标记，

sentences.en: they need to be constructed at a reasonable cost because it's just not right to ask real current generations of real people today to sacrifice through their tax dollars or whatever to invest in protecting a hypothetical intruder into some very far future from a risk for which there's likely no harm to the result.
sentences.zh: 它们必须以合理的成本建造，因为要求当今现实中的人们通过纳税或其他方式做出牺牲，去投资保护某个遥远未来的假想入侵者，使其免受某种很可能不会造成伤害的风险，这是不合理的。

sentences.en: In fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: the panel that met to figure out the WIP marker system was actually not the first instance of thinkers being brought together to consider how to communicate the dangers of nuclear waste over time.
sentences.zh: 负责研究WIPP标记系统的专家组，其实并不是第一次召集思想家来考虑如何跨越时间传达核废料危险性的实例。

sentences.en: There was one such meeting in 1981 for the Yucca Mountain Project, which was eventually scrapped.
sentences.zh: 1981年曾为“尤卡山项目”召开过一次这样的会议，该项目最终被废弃了。

sentences.en: And the Yucca Mountain Project had probably the craziest idea proposed.
sentences.zh: 而尤卡山项目提出的想法可能是最疯狂的。

sentences.en: And even though it was never suggested for WIP, it's become the 99PI in-house favorite method of communicating with people 10,000 years in the future.
sentences.zh: 尽管它从未被提议用于WIPP，但它已成为99PI内部最受欢迎的与一万年后的人们沟通的方法。

sentences.en: In fact, there's probably the reason why we're doing this story at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这可能就是我们做这期节目的原因。

sentences.en: Call it the Raycat solution.
sentences.zh: 称之为“射线猫”（Raycat）解决方案。

sentences.en: My hands-down favorite approach came from these two European philosophers, François Bastide and Paolo Febri.
sentences.zh: 我个人最喜欢的方法来自两位欧洲哲学家：弗朗索瓦·巴斯蒂德和保罗·费布里。

sentences.en: It goes like this.
sentences.zh: 它是这样的。

sentences.en: The two of them got thinking that the most durable thing that humanity has ever made is culture.
sentences.zh: 他们两人开始思考，人类创造出的最持久的东西是文化。

sentences.en: Religion, folklore, belief systems, sure they morph over time, but an essential message can get pulled through.
sentences.zh: 宗教、民间传说、信仰体系，当然它们会随时间演变，但核心信息是可以传承下去的。

sentences.en: And so Bastide and Febri said, here's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 所以巴斯蒂德和费布里说，我们这样做。

sentences.en: We're going to genetically engineer a species of cat that changes color in the presence of radiation.
sentences.zh: 我们要通过基因工程培育一种在辐射环境下会变色的猫。

sentences.en: Then we'd release them out into the wild to become feline Geiger counters.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们放到野外，让它们成为猫咪盖革计数器。

sentences.en: And that's just step number one.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是第一步。

sentences.en: Step number two, we will create an entire system of folklore about these cats.
sentences.zh: 第二步，我们要围绕这些猫创造一套完整的民间传说。

sentences.en: So we will sing songs about them.
sentences.zh: 我们要为它们创作歌曲。

sentences.en: We will draw pictures of them.
sentences.zh: 我们要绘制关于它们的图画。

sentences.en: We will tell stories about them.
sentences.zh: 我们要讲述关于它们的故事。

sentences.en: And like any good story, there's a moral.
sentences.zh: 就像所有好故事一样，这背后有一个寓意。

sentences.en: That when you see the cats turn color, run far, far away.
sentences.zh: 那就是当你看到猫变色时，跑得越远越好。

sentences.en: So don't change color, kitty, keep your color, kitty, stay that midnight black.
sentences.zh: 所以别变色，小猫，保持你的颜色，小猫，保持那午夜般的黑色。

sentences.en: The radiation, the change implies that you kill it, and that's a fact.
sentences.zh: 辐射，这种变化意味着死亡，这是事实。

sentences.en: The radiation, whatever that is, is something we don't want.
sentences.zh: 辐射，无论那是什么，都是我们不想要的。

sentences.en: Because it withers our crops and it burns our skin and it turns our livestock on.
sentences.zh: 因为它会让庄稼枯萎，灼伤我们的皮肤，还会让牲畜变得狂躁。

sentences.en: So don't change color.
sentences.zh: 所以别变色。

sentences.en: Kitty, don't flash your eyes.
sentences.zh: 小猫，别闪烁你的眼睛。

sentences.en: So don't change color.
sentences.zh: 所以别变色。

sentences.en: Once this Raycat folklore becomes embedded into our culture,
sentences.zh: 一旦这些“射线猫”的传说融入我们的文化，

sentences.en: the knowledge it contains can evolve with us, even as our language shifts.
sentences.zh: 其中包含的知识就能与我们共同演化，即使我们的语言发生改变。

sentences.en: 10,000 years from now, these songs and these stories may sound incomprehensible to us,
sentences.zh: 一万年后，这些歌曲和故事听起来可能让我们难以理解，

sentences.en: but as long as they communicate this idea that it's not safe to be where the cats change colors,
sentences.zh: 但只要它们能传达出“猫变色的地方不安全”这一理念，

sentences.en: we will have done our job.
sentences.zh: 我们的任务就完成了。

sentences.en: May the Raycats keep us safe.
sentences.zh: 愿“射线猫”保佑我们平安。

sentences.en: The plan that Sandia Labs decided to move forward with does not involve Raycats, sadly,
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，桑迪亚实验室决定推进的计划并不涉及“射线猫”，

sentences.en: or a landscape of thorns.
sentences.zh: 也不涉及荆棘丛生的景观。

sentences.en: It doesn't even involve the skull and crossbones.
sentences.zh: 甚至连骷髅和交叉骨的标志都没有。

sentences.en: The conceptual design includes a big berm, 30 feet high, earthen construction around the footprint of the repository.
sentences.zh: 其概念设计包括一道巨大的护堤，高30英尺，环绕着储存库的占地范围。

sentences.en: That's Roger Nelson again, the chief scientist overseeing WIPP.
sentences.zh: 说话的还是罗杰·尼尔森，负责监督WIPP项目的首席科学家。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, the powers that be decided to go with solutions that the panelists had pretty much cast aside.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，当权者决定采用那些专家组成员几乎已经否决的方案。

sentences.en: They're marking the area with large granite monuments.
sentences.zh: 他们正在用巨大的花岗岩纪念碑标记该区域。

sentences.en: Large granite monuments at each corner and in the middle and several buried libraries.
sentences.zh: 在每个角落和中间都有巨大的花岗岩纪念碑，还有几个埋在地下的图书馆。

sentences.en: There will be information in seven languages, the six languages of the UN, Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish, and also Navajo.
sentences.zh: 那里将会有七种语言的信息，即联合国的六种工作语言：阿拉伯语、中文、英语、法语、俄语、西班牙语，以及纳瓦霍语。

sentences.en: Because it's the most prevalent indigenous language of the area.
sentences.zh: 因为它是该地区最通用的原住民语言。

sentences.en: The plan is still being finalized.
sentences.zh: 该计划仍在最终敲定中。

sentences.en: But keep in mind, we're talking about protecting people that our great, great, great, great, great, great, great, great, great, great, great grandkids will never know.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，我们谈论的是保护那些我们的玄孙的玄孙的玄孙……永远无法认识的人。

sentences.en: We have a duty to warn them.
sentences.zh: 我们有义务警告他们。

sentences.en: We have a responsibility to mark the area.
sentences.zh: 我们有责任标记该区域。

sentences.en: After a certain point, I started wondering, like, isn't this just a bit ridiculous?
sentences.zh: 到了一定程度，我开始怀疑，这难道不是有点荒谬吗？

sentences.en: While I was researching this story, I read about this town called Tallahassee, a small, predominantly African-American community, about an hour, hour and a half south of Tampa,
sentences.zh: 在研究这个故事时，我读到了一个叫塔拉哈西的小镇，那是一个以非裔美国人为主的小社区，位于坦帕以南大约一小时到一小时半的车程处，

sentences.en: Florida.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, a beryllium processing plant was set up in the middle of town.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代，一家铍加工厂在镇中心建立起来。

sentences.en: The plant manufactured components for nuclear bombs and also built pieces of the Hubble Space Telescope.
sentences.zh: 该工厂为核弹制造零部件，也制造哈勃太空望远镜的部件。

sentences.en: Anyway, it turned out that this plant was never very good about dealing with its waste.
sentences.zh: 总之，事实证明这家工厂在处理废料方面一直做得不好。

sentences.en: Beryllium dust and other toxins made their way into the town's groundwater.
sentences.zh: 铍粉尘和其他毒素进入了镇上的地下水。

sentences.en: And Tallahassee had always gotten its water from shallow wells.
sentences.zh: 而塔拉哈西一直是从浅水井取水。

sentences.en: Residents started noticing that a lot of people were getting diagnosed with cancer and other diseases, including berylliosis, which you get from exposure to beryllium.
sentences.zh: 居民们开始注意到，很多人被诊断出患有癌症和其他疾病，包括铍中毒，这是由于接触铍引起的。

sentences.en: Tallahassee filed a lawsuit against the company that owns the plant, Lockheed Martin.
sentences.zh: 塔拉哈西对拥有该工厂的公司洛克希德·马丁公司提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: And Lockheed spent years dragging out the lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 而洛克希德公司花了数年时间拖延诉讼。

sentences.en: Now, the reason I bring this up is because Lockheed Martin happens to be the parent company of Sandia National Labs, the corporation that runs the Whip site over in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 我提到这一点是因为洛克希德·马丁公司恰好是桑迪亚国家实验室的母公司，也就是在新墨西哥州运营WIPP站点的公司。

sentences.en: And this case at Tallahassee is hardly unique.
sentences.zh: 而塔拉哈西的这个案例绝非个例。

sentences.en: There are literally thousands of towns across the United States, many of them low income or communities of color, that have become contaminated in similar ways.
sentences.zh: 在美国各地，有成千上万个城镇，其中许多是低收入或有色人种社区，都以类似的方式受到了污染。

sentences.en: And so the 10,000 year Whip marker system feels really noble, but maybe a little misguided.
sentences.zh: 所以，一万年的WIPP标记系统感觉非常高尚，但可能有点误入歧途。

sentences.en: I am all for taking care of people 10,000 years in the future.
sentences.zh: 我完全支持照顾一万年后的人们。

sentences.en: But I think the best way to do that is to start taking care of people that are alive today.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最好的方法是先照顾好今天活着的人。

sentences.en: That way, there might be humans in 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 这样，一万年后才可能还有人类存在。

sentences.en: And cats.
sentences.zh: 还有猫。
